insights.headline: Gold heads for its worst week since March as Fed hike bets and the AI rout drive a slide to near $3,500
insights.summary: Spot gold held near $3,500 after falling for a fifth straight day, on track for its worst week since March. MCX gold traded near Rs 1.22 lakh per 10 g and silver near Rs 1.48 lakh per kg, with silver down about 65% from its January peak against gold's 37%. A hawkish Fed, a firm dollar and AI-led selling drove the rout, while wedding-season buyers returned as prices eased.
points: Spot gold held near $3,500 after a fifth straight daily fall, on track for its worst week since March at about 8%.
MCX gold traded near Rs 1.22 lakh per 10 g and silver near Rs 1.48 lakh per kg, far below January record highs.
Fed hike bets reached 97% for December as officials signalled more increases, Investing.com reports.
Silver has fallen about 65% from its January peak against gold's 37%, Mint reports, as wedding buyers return.
DSP Mutual Fund has turned bullish on bullion after the crash, rebuilding exposure at set price levels, Mint reports.

brief.headline: Gold holds near $3,514 after worst week since March
brief.summary: Spot gold held near $3,514 after a 9% weekly slide; MCX gold at Rs 1.22 lakh per 10 g, silver near Rs 1.48 lakh per kg.

bullets.text: Fed rate-hike bets, a firmer dollar and rising yields drove the selloff, with the AI-led equity rout forcing liquidations, FXEmpire says.
On MCX, gold is 37% and silver 65% below January record highs, Mint reports, while the slide relieved households with weddings ahead.
US core PCE inflation lands on November 25 at 7:00 pm IST, the next test of the Fed's rate path before its December 9 decision.

trending.title: Worst week since March
trending.summary: Gold slid for a fifth day to near $3,500 as hawkish Fed bets, a firm dollar and the AI equity rout forced selling across metals, putting the metal on course for its worst week since March.

trending.title: Silver's steeper slide
trending.summary: Silver has fallen about 65% from its January peak, far more than gold's 37%, with MCX silver near Rs 1.48 lakh per kg and silver ETFs at 52-week lows.

trending.title: Wedding-season relief
trending.summary: Lower prices are bringing householders and jewellers back ahead of weddings, while festive demand picks up after the sharp correction.

trending.title: A fund steps back in
trending.summary: DSP Mutual Fund has turned bullish after the crash and is rebuilding bullion exposure at preset price levels, a counterpoint to a week of forced selling.

trending.title: Rupee's strong month
trending.summary: The rupee is set for its best monthly gain in eight years on strong foreign fund inflows, even as India's forex reserves fell to a three-month low of $705 billion.

items.title: Gold price continues to fall as AI selloff, rate-hike bets weigh. What’s ahead?
items.summary: Spot gold fell 3% to $3,514.08 an ounce on Friday, touching a 14-month low of $3,502.49, and has shed about 9.4% this week — its worst week since March. Hawkish Fed signals and an AI-led equity selloff drove the slide, with markets pricing a 96% chance of a December rate hike. Silver fell 4.1% to $40.99 an ounce, while analysts said a bottom could come sooner rather than later.

items.title: Gold Set for Worst Week Since March on Hawkish Fed, AI Selloff
items.summary: Gold fell for a fifth straight day to near $3,500 an ounce, heading for its biggest weekly drop since March at about 8%, Bloomberg reports, as a hawkish Fed signalled more rate hikes and the AI stock rout forced selling across metals; silver has fallen almost 15% over five sessions.

items.title: Gold vs silver price crash compared: White metal loses 65%, gold sheds 37% from record highs
items.summary: Gold has fallen 37% and silver 65% from their January 29 record highs on MCX, Mint reports, with gold at Rs 1.22 lakh per 10 g and silver near Rs 1.47 lakh per kg after Friday's slide; investors who bought in October 2025 still hold small gains in both metals.

items.title: Gold, silver prices crash: MCX gold nears ₹1.21 lakh, silver plunges ₹10,614/kg; here’s why
items.summary: MCX gold fell 4.7% to an intraday low of Rs 1,21,424 per 10 g and silver 6.7% to Rs 1,46,868 per kg on Friday, as a dollar at a 19-month high and bets on a December Fed hike hit bullion. COMEX gold traded 3.6% lower at $3,551.60 an ounce, with US Treasury yields above 5%.

items.title: Gold Sinks To One-Year Low, Silver Plunges Rs 2.46 lakh From Record High
items.summary: Delhi gold of 99.9% purity fell Rs 5,200 to Rs 1,29,300 per 10 g on Friday, its lowest in a year, while silver dropped Rs 4,000 to Rs 1.58 lakh per kg — Rs 2.46 lakh below its January record of Rs 4.04 lakh; spot gold slid to $3,515 an ounce.

items.title: Gold Hits 15-Month Low, Silver Drops Near Rs 1.48 Lakh | Three Reasons Why Precious Metals Are Crashing?
items.summary: MCX gold fell 3.84% to Rs 1,22,561 per 10 g and silver slid 5.99% to Rs 1,48,050 per kg, NDTV Profit reported, as both metals hit 15-month lows. Gold has lost Rs 4,891 per 10 g and silver Rs 9,432 per kg in the session.

items.title: Gold Price Crash Tests $3,500 as Fed Hike Bets Reach 97%
items.summary: Gold tested the $3,500 level, touching an overnight low of $3,514.50, as markets priced a 97.3% chance of a quarter-point Fed hike at the December 8-9 meeting. Spot gold traded at $3,568.65, heading for a weekly loss of about 9%, its steepest in eight months, while silver fell 14% on the week to $42.15.

items.title: Wall Street stays bearish after gold's slide to $3,500, Main Street pessimism deepens ahead of holiday week
items.summary: Gold suffered another brutal weekly decline to a low of $3,502.93 an ounce, Kitco News reported, as hawkish Fed expectations, surging Treasury yields and a stronger dollar overwhelmed safe-haven demand. The Kitco survey showed Wall Street still bearish and Main Street bulls down to 36%, with 46% expecting further losses; PCE inflation, GDP and jobless claims are due Wednesday before Thanksgiving.

items.title: Gold (XAUUSD), Silver, Platinum Forecasts – Gold Tests New Lows Amid Panic In Markets
items.summary: Gold is testing new lows as the sell-off continues, FXEmpire said, with traders focused on the AI-led pullback in US equities and markets in panic mode. Gold is trying to settle below support at $3,500-$3,520, with the next support at $3,400-$3,420; the chance of a 50-basis-point December hike has fallen to zero, while Treasury yields eased and the dollar pulled back from yearly highs.

items.title: Silver Weekly Price Forecast: Silver Continues to Fight Real Yields
items.summary: Silver broke below $45 and its 200-week moving average as rising real yields and weaker speculative positioning point to a deeper slide toward $40, FXEmpire says. The Silver Institute and Metals Focus still project a 35-million-ounce global deficit this year, but industrial demand is forecast to fall 3%.

items.title: Gold price crash: Yellow metal and silver slump over 4% each on MCX
items.summary: Gold fell nearly 4% to about Rs 1.22 lakh per 10 g on MCX and silver slid nearly 6% to Rs 1.48 lakh per kg as the sell-off deepened, CNBC-TV18 reported. A strengthening dollar and rising expectations of a US Federal Reserve rate hike drove the slide, with spot gold at $3,551.68, down 8.9% on the week.

items.title: Gold, silver price crash: DSP Mutual Fund turns bullish on bullion, reveals new buying strategy; check price levels
items.summary: DSP Mutual Fund has turned bullish on bullion after the crash and is rebuilding exposure in its multi-asset fund of funds, adding gold at preset levels — 0.5% more for every $100 fall below $3,850 an ounce — and silver 0.5% more for every $2 fall below $47, Mint reports. DSP puts fair value at $4,484 for gold and $64 for silver. Spot gold fell 3% on Friday to $3,514.08, a 14-month low.

items.title: MCX Gold Sinks 40% From All-Time High: Analysts Flag The One Level Traders Must Watch
items.summary: MCX gold December futures fell 2.03% to Rs 1,22,659 per 10 g on Friday, with silver down 4.96% to Rs 1,49,673 per kg, and NDTV Profit reports gold is now over 40% below its all-time high after a fifth straight losing session; analysts cited in the piece watch $3,500 an ounce as the key support for spot gold.

items.title: GJC alerts BIS over suspected gold adulteration, urges jewellers to tighten quality checks
items.summary: The All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council has alerted the Bureau of Indian Standards over reports of rhenium- and iridium-based alloys being used to add weight to gold jewellery without matching purity. GJC said BIS is taking the matter seriously, urged jewellers to tighten quality checks, and asked buyers to verify hallmarks on the BIS Care app and insist on GST-paid invoices.

items.title: Householders With Weddings Relieved As Gold, Silver Prices Slide
items.summary: Families in Telangana with weddings ahead welcomed the slide after months of record prices, with many who had postponed jewellery purchases now willing to buy, while bullion traders worry about the falling value of their stocks; the paper attributes the drop largely to developments in international markets.

items.title: Gold, silver price correction spurs jewellery demand ahead of wedding season
items.summary: A sharp correction in gold and silver has brought buyers back to jewellery stores ahead of the peak wedding season, jewellers say. A Rajkot jeweller said the fall was steeper than the market expected and put any further downside at 2-5%, while silver has largely returned to year-ago levels. Retail buyers say lower prices have eased the cost of wedding purchases.

items.title: Gold under a hiking Fed: central-bank demand versus real rates
items.summary: Kitco's commentary argues real yields, not the dollar alone, are driving gold's slide, with December hike odds near 96% and the 10-year real yield near 2.9%; central banks bought 321 tonnes in the third quarter, 42% more than a year earlier, but that buying runs on a slower clock than the rates market.

items.title: Gold Price Outlook: Goldman Sachs Sees Gold At $4,650 By 2027-End; Central Bank Buying To Drive
items.summary: Goldman Sachs sees gold reaching $4,650 an ounce by the end of 2027, with continued central-bank buying driving the recovery. The call comes even as gold trades near 14-month lows under pressure from expectations of further US rate hikes.

items.title: Gold price falls nears $3,500 as miners face soaring costs
items.summary: All-in sustaining costs jumped 22% year on year in Q2 to $1,930 an ounce, the steepest rise since 2013, squeezing margins as gold slid toward $3,500. Sustaining capital spending hit a record $441 an ounce, up 34% on the quarter, and the margin above costs fell 16% to $2,582 an ounce. Barrick realised $174 less per ounce in Q3 and the VanEck Gold Miners ETF fell 12% on the week.

items.title: 18K gold slips below Rs 1 lakh, down 8% in three days: Is it a buying opportunity?
items.summary: IBJA 18K gold has stayed below Rs 1 lakh per 10 g for three straight sessions, falling 8.06% to Rs 92,688 from Rs 1,00,814 on November 17, as a stronger dollar, higher bond yields and Fed tightening bets pressured bullion. IBJA put 24K gold at Rs 1,23,584 and 22K at Rs 1,13,203 per 10 g.

items.title: Gold ETFs down 5%; Silver ETFs plunge over 6%, trade at 52-week lows
items.summary: Gold ETFs fell 5% and silver ETFs plunged over 6% to 52-week lows, Business Standard reported, as bullion prices crashed. Gold futures traded up to 4% lower around $3,530 and silver futures near $41.60, down nearly 6%, on fears of a December Fed rate hike, a stronger dollar and rising bond yields.

items.title: Rupee set for best monthly gain in 8 years on strong foreign fund inflows
items.summary: The rupee has gained 2.46% so far in November to 92.68 per dollar, its best monthly rise in eight years, helped by nearly $13 billion in foreign inflows, lower crude prices and exporter dollar sales. It rose 0.67% on Friday, crossing 93 for the first time since April.

items.title: India's forex reserves fall to over three month low of $705 billion
items.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves fell more than $14 billion in the week to November 13 to $705.3 billion, the lowest in about three months, RBI data showed, with foreign currency assets down $7.8 billion and the value of the central bank's gold holdings down $6.1 billion. The rupee strengthened on Friday to 92.67 per dollar, its strongest since April.
